scenario: Marketing wants every click from the shop at 20,000 events a second on sale days, read live by a dashboard and also archived for the data team.
options: A Service Bus queue, because it guarantees delivery
A table in the orders database
Event Hubs, with a consumer group per reader and Capture for the archive
Event Grid custom topic
explanation: High-volume facts read by several independent readers, with replay and archiving, are an event stream. A queue delivers each message to one reader and is not built for this volume, a database table fights the checkout for locks, and Event Grid pushes discrete notifications rather than retaining a stream.

scenario: The dashboard job and the fraud function both read the clickstream using the $Default consumer group. Each seems to see only about half the events.
stem: Why, and what is the fix?
options: Event Hubs drops half the events under load; add throughput units
They are splitting the partitions within one consumer group; give each application its own consumer group
The retention period is too short
The partition key is wrong
explanation: Within a consumer group, partitions are shared among readers, so two different applications in one group each get part of the stream. A consumer group per application gives each its own complete view and position.

scenario: A hub on the Standard tier was created with 2 partitions. The fraud function now needs 8 parallel instances to keep up.
options: Nothing; add instances and they will share the load
Only 2 instances in the consumer group can read in parallel, and on Standard the partition count cannot be changed; a new hub with more partitions is needed
Add throughput units to create more partitions
Change the partition key
explanation: Parallelism within a consumer group is capped by the number of partitions, and on Standard that number is fixed at creation. Extra instances would sit idle. Throughput units add capacity, not partitions. That is why partitions are chosen generously up front.

scenario: Every event is sent with the partition key 'shop'. Producers receive ServerBusy errors although total traffic is well under the namespace's capacity.
options: A constant key sends every event to one partition, which becomes hot; use a high-cardinality key such as the session ID, or no key
The namespace needs Premium tier
Retention is too long
The consumers are checkpointing too often
explanation: The key decides the partition, so one value means one partition doing all the work while the others idle. A key with many distinct values, such as sessionId, spreads the load and still keeps each session in order.

scenario: After a redeploy, the fraud function processes a burst of events it has already seen.
options: No; Event Hubs guarantees exactly-once delivery
Yes: consumers resume from their last checkpoint and re-read everything since, so processing must be idempotent
No; it means retention is misconfigured
Yes, but only on the Basic tier
explanation: Checkpoints are saved periodically, not per event, so a restart replays events since the last checkpoint. That is normal at-least-once behaviour; the consumer must tolerate it. Checkpointing more often reduces the replay but costs storage operations.

scenario: A consumer was down for four days during an incident. The hub keeps events for three days.
stem: What would have protected the missing day?
options: More partitions
Event Hubs Capture writing the stream to the data lake, so older events can be reprocessed from files
A second consumer group
Auto-inflate
explanation: Events older than the retention period are gone from the hub. Capture keeps a complete copy in storage, which can be replayed or analysed later. Partitions, consumer groups and auto-inflate do not extend how long events are kept.

scenario: A developer suggests sending ReserveStock commands through the clickstream event hub, since it is already there and fast.
options: Event Hubs cannot carry JSON
Event Hubs has no per-message acknowledgement, locks or dead-lettering; commands that must each be processed belong on a Service Bus queue
Commands are too large for Event Hubs
Event Hubs is only for Azure services' own events
explanation: A stream is a log of facts that consumers read by position. There is no way to say 'this particular command failed, retry it or dead-letter it'. Service Bus provides exactly those per-message guarantees for work that matters.

scenario: The React team proposes sending click events straight from the browser to Event Hubs using a connection string in the front-end code.
options: Use the connection string but mark it read-only
Send events to a small telemetry API that batches them and publishes to Event Hubs with its managed identity
Send each click as a separate HTTP request directly to Event Hubs
Store clicks in local storage and upload them weekly
explanation: Anything in the front-end bundle is public, so an Event Hubs key there lets anyone flood or pollute the stream. A backend collector validates, batches and publishes with a managed identity. Per-click requests waste capacity, and a send key is never read-only in the sense that would help.
